raw_case_text:
The 23-year-old primigest mother had no pregnancy-related complications. Prenatal care was done regularly at a private clinic with unremarkable serology in the first semester: Hepatitis B, HIV, and syphilis negative. She had flu-like syndrome and an episode of fever (38.5 C) 2 days prior to admission. At arrival, she was afebrile and COVID-19 rapid antigen test was negative. She was admitted for unspecified sepsis during labor and treated with ampicillin for 5 days. During her stay, the initial investigation demonstrated an isolated elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) of 130 mg/L. Complete blood count (CBC) was normal, with leucocytes 4.4 x 109/L, platelets 223 x 109/L, and hemoglobin 115 g/L. Urine examination was normal, and hemoculture later was proven negative. Dengue serology was negative. Few hours after admission, the delivery was spontaneous and uneventful.
At Special Care Nursery, the infant was active and pink, with good sucking. The physical examination was unremarkable. Due to the possible risks of perinatal infection, a septic workup was done and showed a normal leucocyte count (11.4 x 109/L), with an absolute neutrophil count of 7.2 x 109/L, lymphocytes of 2.3 x 109/L (20%) and immature to total neutrophil ratio (I/T ratio) 0.01; hemoglobin and platelets were within the normal range (Table 1). Inflammatory markers, however, were elevated: CRP of 34.64 mg/L and procalcitonin (PCT) of 1.48 mcg/L. Per unit protocol for suspected early-onset sepsis, empiric antibiotics including Ampicillin and Cefotaxime were initiated.
At Day 3 of life, the infant started to develop morbilliform rash with petechiae, predominantly found over the back (Figure 1), and intermittent nocturnal fever (38 C). Vital signs were stable. There were neither neurological signs nor hepatosplenomegaly. No mosquito bite marks were reported. Control blood tests showed decreased platelets (78 x 109/L) and increased CRP (43 mg/L). Syphilis tests were nonreactive. Hemoculture and gastric aspirate done at admission were negative. Brain ultrasound, done before Lumbar Puncture (LP), showed no bleeding signs. Heart ultrasound showed no defect. The second blood culture was drawn, and LP was done, with normal results: leucocytes 06/mm3, albumin 0.5 g/L, and glucose 0.79 g/L. Based upon local guidelines, the clinicians upgraded the antibiotics to second line: Meropenem and Amikacin.
About 48 h later, because of the persistently on-off fever and progressively decreasing platelets, we interviewed parents by phone during the restricted period amid COVID pandemic to get more detailed information before any further investigations. According to the mother about 2 days after delivery, she started developing rash, with low-grade fever and persistent arthralgia. Given the information, we decided to rule out other mosquito-borne congenital infections, in an early stage, by combined PCR, which later confirmed the diagnosis of congenital chikungunya (Table 2).
Early-onset neonatal sepsis, culture not proven
Hypoproliferative thrombocytopenia, associated with small-for-gestational-age neonates
Mosquito-borne congenital infection such as congenital dengue
The treatment was supportive. Apyrexia was noted on day 6 of life. Antibiotics were discontinued 7 days after the negativation of the second blood culture. Platelets increased progressively to 112 x 109/L at the discharge (Day 10). She was brought for a follow-up on day 20, with good weight gain and normalized platelets. The girl will be follow up every 3 months until the age of 2 years, following our local follow-up program for low birth weight.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 3-day-old female neonate developed intermittent nocturnal fever and a morbilliform petechial rash.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A female neonate was delivered spontaneously and uneventfully to a mother admitted with intrapartum fever and elevated CRP. At birth, the infant was active and sucking well. On day 3 of life, she developed intermittent nocturnal fever (38 °C) and a morbilliform rash with petechiae predominantly on the back, accompanied by falling platelet counts.
subjective.past_medical_history: Born to a 23-year-old primigravida mother who experienced flu-like illness and fever (38.5 °C) 2 days prior to delivery, and developed rash, low-grade fever, and persistent arthralgia 2 days postpartum; maternal prenatal serologies (HBV, HIV, syphilis, COVID-19 rapid antigen) were negative. No documented mosquito bites on the infant.

objective.physical_examination: At birth: Active, pink, good sucking reflex, physical examination unremarkable. On day 3: Temperature 38 °C; vital signs stable; morbilliform rash with petechiae predominantly over the back; no neurological abnormalities; no hepatosplenomegaly; no mosquito bite marks.
objective.routine_investigations: Birth labs: Leucocytes 11.4 x 10^9/L (absolute neutrophil count 7.2 x 10^9/L, lymphocytes 2.3 x 10^9/L [20%], I/T ratio 0.01), hemoglobin and platelets normal; CRP 34.64 mg/L; procalcitonin 1.48 mcg/L. Day 3 labs: Platelets decreased to 78 x 10^9/L, CRP increased to 43 mg/L, increasing later to 112 x 10^9/L at discharge. Blood cultures (initial and repeat) and gastric aspirate culture: negative. Syphilis serology: non-reactive. Bedside cranial ultrasound: No intracranial hemorrhage. Echocardiogram: Normal / no structural defect.
objective.advanced_workup: Lumbar puncture / CSF analysis: Leucocytes 6/mm3, albumin 0.5 g/L, glucose 0.79 g/L (normal).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Confirmation: Combined PCR testing confirmed vertical / congenital Chikungunya virus infection; maternal dengue serology and infant workup for congenital dengue were negative. Other differential diagnoses considered included culture-negative early-onset neonatal sepsis and small-for-gestational-age hypoproliferative thrombocytopenia. Management and course: Managed initially with ampicillin and cefotaxime, upgraded on day 3 to meropenem and amikacin; antibiotics discontinued 7 days after negative second blood culture. Apyrexia achieved by day 6; platelets rose to 112 x 10^9/L at discharge (day 10). At day 20 follow-up, she exhibited good weight gain and normalized platelets.
